scope: Episode 01 major external, dated, technical, comparative, safety and empirical claims; narrative examples and pedagogical hypotheses separately identified

ANTHROPIC_AGENTS.specific_finding: Reports experience with agent workflows, explicitly differentiates predetermined workflows from agent-decided processes; recommends simple compositional patterns.
ANTHROPIC_AGENTS.limitations: Vendor-authored engineering experience, not a controlled scientific comparison or independent replication.

OPENAI_AGENT_EVALS.specific_finding: Documents end-to-end traces, tool calls, graders, datasets and evaluation runs for observing and evaluating agent behaviour.
OPENAI_AGENT_EVALS.limitations: Product documentation is normative and changes with platform versions; it does not prove effects of any architecture.

OPENAI_FEB2026.specific_finding: OpenAI reports SWE-bench Verified contamination and test defects, describes audit sample and benchmark-validity concerns.
OPENAI_FEB2026.limitations: OpenAI-led audit of selected failure cases; its own claims and methods need independent scrutiny.

OPENAI_JUL2026.specific_finding: Audit of 731 SWE-bench Pro public tasks found estimated 30 percent defective tasks; OpenAI explicitly withdrew its recommendation of Pro.
OPENAI_JUL2026.limitations: A vendor-led audit using a partly flagged subset and independent engineers; estimate depends on methodology, task mix, and definition of broken.

AGENTBENCH.specific_finding: Introduces multi-environment interactive agent benchmarking, measuring sequential decisions beyond isolated question answering.
AGENTBENCH.limitations: Historical preprint benchmark; models and environments may be superseded; scores are benchmark-dependent.

AGENTJUDGEBENCH.specific_finding: Reports degraded reliability of LLM judging on complex agent tool-call workflow graphs and benefit of structured rubrics in some conditions.
AGENTJUDGEBENCH.limitations: Preprint with limited generators/judges and its own benchmark design; not a universal failure-rate estimate.

MOSAIC_ICML.specific_finding: Reports empirical guard training against dangerous multi-step tool use, prompt injection and privacy leakage across several systems.
MOSAIC_ICML.limitations: Results specific to the evaluated models, benchmarks, threat models and experimental setup.

LLM_JUDGE_SURVEY.specific_finding: Systematically reviews known reliability, consistency and bias problems with model-based grading.
LLM_JUDGE_SURVEY.limitations: Survey and preprint; not independent experimental validation of every cited mitigation.

claims.excerpt: An agent adds an action loop.
claims.limitations: A conceptual definition; the literature uses varying boundaries between scripted workflows and autonomous agents.

claims.excerpt: If every action is predetermined, you have a workflow, even if a language model appears within it.
claims.limitations: This is one influential operational distinction, not a universally adopted formal definition of agent.

claims.excerpt: A tool name is not a guarantee of correctness.
claims.limitations: Illustrative engineering warning; correctness depends on schema, argument validation, execution and independent results.

claims.excerpt: Context engineering is the design of what the model receives, when it receives it, and how that information is selected or compressed.
claims.limitations: A working engineering definition, not a measured claim that any particular context policy outperforms another.

claims.excerpt: In an agentic system, a plan is valuable when it improves decisions in the environment.
claims.limitations: General hypothesis motivating an ablation; the podcast does not present evidence that planning always improves task success.

claims.excerpt: A strong environment gives the agent ways to falsify its own hypothesis, not merely ways to confirm it.
claims.limitations: Prescriptive design principle; tool-feedback benefits must be independently tested for each environment.

claims.excerpt: Two agents can share the same mistaken assumption.
claims.limitations: Plausible correlated-error scenario, not a quantitative measured multi-agent failure rate.

claims.excerpt: In February twenty twenty-six, OpenAI published a critique of SWE-bench Verified
claims.limitations: The original February announcement was subsequently followed by a July audit of the recommended replacement.

claims.excerpt: In July twenty twenty-six, OpenAI published a follow-up audit of SWE-bench Pro
claims.limitations: OpenAI's own analysis; estimated defect rate and retraction should not be extrapolated to all coding benchmarks.

claims.excerpt: OpenAI explicitly withdrew its earlier recommendation.
claims.limitations: Refers specifically to SWE-bench Pro and the July 2026 recommendation withdrawal.

claims.excerpt: A model judging its own answer is not independent verification.
claims.limitations: Model grading may still be useful, but not independent objective evidence without calibration or other verification.

claims.excerpt: A trajectory records the observations, tool calls, edits, tests, and decision points in an agent run.
claims.limitations: This is a useful trace abstraction, though actual trace schema and instrumentation vary between systems.

claims.excerpt: One especially important risk is prompt injection.
claims.limitations: A general safety-risk category; prevalence and severity depend on exposure, privilege controls and attacker capability.

claims.excerpt: The agent does not need malicious intent to exploit a poorly designed success metric.
claims.limitations: Reward-hacking example is hypothetical in this episode; no direct experiment quantifying this exact failure is reported.

claims.excerpt: Every extra model call consumes tokens.
claims.limitations: Token use and billing vary by model, provider, cached context and runtime; no specific monetary savings claimed.

claims.excerpt: At the end, write one paragraph with four parts: the question, the controlled comparison, the observed result, and the remaining uncertainty.
claims.limitations: A teaching recommendation, not a validated universal structure for all research reports.
